title: Workbench with open black instrument, monitor and QDK poster
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.
One computer monitor is visible at the front-left of the image, placed on the near desk and displaying a dark circular image on-screen.
One standard keyboard and one computer mouse are visible on the near desk in front of the monitor.
One black box-style instrument with a hinged lid open is on the corner of the bench to the right of the monitor; the lid is propped open and internal components and cables are visible.
Two small optical posts/mounts (short cylindrical stands) are visible on the near desk between the monitor and the black instrument.
One thin curved tube or fibre cable extends from the black instrument across the bench toward the right-side table; the portion visible is curved and enters the frame from the instrument.
Several loose cables and a coiled power/extension cable are visible on and under the right-side table (multiple cables present but exact count cannot be determined).
One large blue-and-white wall poster consisting of multiple panels titled 'Quantum Demonstrator Kit (QDK)' is mounted on the wall above the right-side bench.
Two cardboard boxes containing papers and small items are on the right-side bench; one box is open with loose papers visible.
One flat rectangular object that appears to be a closed laptop or thin device is on the right-side bench beneath some cables (identification uncertain).
One small rectangular remote or phone-like object and one power strip or similar rectangular electronic item are on the right-side bench next to the boxes.
spatial_relations: A large window with a glass partition occupies the left-middle background; through it a corridor and a glass door with a vertical 'PULL' sign are visible.
The monitor and keyboard are placed on a near white desk at the bottom-left of the image; the open black instrument sits on the adjoining corner of that desk to the right of the monitor.
The black instrument's lid is open and hinged toward the back-left; optical posts are arranged in front of and slightly to the right of the monitor near the instrument.
A separate right-side bench or table runs along the right wall beneath the QDK poster; on that bench are boxes, cables, and the small rectangular device (possible laptop).
Cables from the black instrument run across the corner area and toward the items on the right-side bench; several cables and a coiled power extension lie on or under that bench.
The QDK poster is mounted on the wall above the right-side bench, roughly centered over that workspace.

The monitor bezel and keyboard are black; cables are predominantly black and white.
